why: Picking the lower middle of each sorted segment as the root is the 'sorted array to balanced BST' construction; the preorder can be emitted directly by recursing on index ranges, and the special-value test is applied to each value as it is emitted.
hints: You never need node objects: a subtree is just a range [lo, hi] of the sorted array.
For range [lo, hi] the root is index lo + (hi - lo) // 2; emit it, then the left range, then the right range.
Use a stack of ranges (push right before left) and output 0 for values where x//10 + (x//10)*(x%10) + x%10 == x. O(n log n) for the sort.
pitfalls: Lower middle: for even length take the left of the two middles.
Keep duplicates when sorting; do not use a set.
Replace values only in the output; the tree shape comes from the original sorted values.
